# Paired t-test sample size calculation
# H0: mean weight reduction = 0 vs H1: mean weight reduction = 3 kg
# One-sided test, alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.80

# Parameters
mean_diff <- 3        # kg - hypothesized mean weight reduction
sd_baseline <- 5      # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5    # kg
rho <- 0.5            # within-person correlation

# Calculate SD of paired differences
# σ_diff = √(σ₀² + σ₁² − 2ρσ₀σ₁)
sd_diff <- sqrt(sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2*rho*sd_baseline*sd_followup)
cat("SD of paired differences:", sd_diff, "kg\n")

# Effect size (Cohen's d for paired t-test)
cohen_d <- mean_diff / sd_diff
cat("Cohen's d:", cohen_d, "\n\n")

# For one-sided paired t-test: n = 2 * (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 / d^2
# where z_alpha is critical value for one-sided test at alpha level
# and z_beta is critical value for (1-power)
# But for small samples, use exact t-distribution approach via power.t.test

# Try using stats::power.t.test for paired t-test
# This function can invert to find sample size

# For a paired t-test with power.t.test:
# - type = "paired" for paired test
# - delta = effect size (mean difference)
# - sd = SD of differences
# - sig.level = alpha
# - power = target power
# - alternative = "one.sided"

result_80 <- power.t.test(
  n = NULL,           # We're solving for n
  delta = mean_diff,  # Effect size (mean difference)
  sd = sd_diff,       # SD of paired differences
  sig.level = 0.05,   # One-sided alpha
  power = 0.80,       # Target power
  type = "paired",    # Paired t-test
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

print(result_80)
cat("\nContinuous solution (n):", result_80$n, "\n")

# Since we need integer participants, round up
n_rounded <- ceiling(result_80$n)
cat("Rounded up to integer:", n_rounded, "\n\n")

# Verify the achieved power at the rounded sample size
power_achieved <- power.t.test(
  n = n_rounded,
  delta = mean_diff,
  sd = sd_diff,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  type = "paired",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("ACHIEVED POWER at n =", n_rounded, ":", power_achieved$power, "\n")

# Also check the previous integer (n-1) to confirm it doesn't meet target
if(n_rounded > 1) {
  power_prev <- power.t.test(
    n = n_rounded - 1,
    delta = mean_diff,
    sd = sd_diff,
    sig.level = 0.05,
    type = "paired",
    alternative = "one.sided"
  )
  cat("Power at n =", n_rounded - 1, ":", power_prev$power, "\n")
}

# Summary
cat("\n=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size:", n_rounded, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_achieved$power, 4), "\n")
cat("Target power: 0.80\n")
cat("Meets target:", power_achieved$power >= 0.80, "\n")

# Independent verification of paired t-test sample size calculation
# Using alternative approach and detailed formula checks

# Given parameters
mean_diff <- 3        # kg (hypothesized mean weight reduction)
sd_baseline <- 5      # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5    # kg
rho <- 0.5            # within-person correlation
alpha <- 0.05         # one-sided significance level
target_power <- 0.80

# Step 1: Verify SD of differences formula
# For paired differences: σ_diff = √(σ₀² + σ₁² − 2ρσ₀σ₁)
sd_diff_formula <- sqrt(sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2*rho*sd_baseline*sd_followup)
cat("Step 1: SD of paired differences\n")
cat("Formula: σ_diff = √(σ₀² + σ₁² − 2ρσ₀σ₁)\n")
cat("Calculation: √(5² + 5.5² − 2×0.5×5×5.5)\n")
cat("           = √(25 + 30.25 − 27.5)\n")
cat("           = √27.75\n")
cat("Result: σ_diff =", sd_diff_formula, "kg\n\n")

# Step 2: Calculate Cohen's d
cohen_d <- mean_diff / sd_diff_formula
cat("Step 2: Effect size (Cohen's d for paired design)\n")
cat("Cohen's d = 3 / ", sd_diff_formula, " =", cohen_d, "\n\n")

# Step 3: Manual power calculation using non-central t-distribution
# For one-sided test at α = 0.05:
# Critical value t_crit from standard t distribution with (n-1) df
# Non-centrality parameter: λ = d * √n = (mean_diff / sd_diff) * √n

# Test for various sample sizes to find minimum meeting target power
cat("Step 3: Power calculation across sample sizes\n")
cat("n\tCritical t\tNon-centrality λ\tPower (via pt)\n")
cat(strrep("-", 60), "\n")

powers_manual <- data.frame(n = integer(), power = numeric())

for (n in 18:23) {
  df <- n - 1  # degrees of freedom for one-sample/paired t-test
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)  # one-sided critical value (upper tail)
  lambda <- cohen_d * sqrt(n)   # non-centrality parameter
  
  # Power = P(T > t_crit | λ) = 1 - P(T ≤ t_crit | λ)
  # where T ~ t(df, λ) non-central t-distribution
  power_manual <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  
  powers_manual <- rbind(powers_manual, 
                         data.frame(n = n, power = power_manual))
  
  cat(n, "\t", round(t_crit, 4), "\t\t", 
      round(lambda, 4), "\t\t\t", 
      round(power_manual, 6), "\n")
}

cat("\n")

# Step 4: Verify using power.t.test
cat("Step 4: Verification using R's power.t.test\n")
for (n in 20:21) {
  result <- power.t.test(
    n = n,
    delta = mean_diff,
    sd = sd_diff_formula,
    sig.level = 0.05,
    type = "paired",
    alternative = "one.sided"
  )
  cat("n =", n, ": power =", round(result$power, 6), "\n")
}

cat("\n")

# Step 5: Inversion to find exact continuous solution
cat("Step 5: Sample size inversion for target power 80%\n")
result_invert <- power.t.test(
  n = NULL,
  delta = mean_diff,
  sd = sd_diff_formula,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  power = target_power,
  type = "paired",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)
cat("Continuous solution: n =", result_invert$n, "participants\n")
cat("Ceiling (minimum integer): n =", ceiling(result_invert$n), "participants\n\n")

result_min <- power.t.test(
  n = n_min,
  delta = mean_diff,
  sd = sd_diff_formula,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  type = "paired",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)
result_prev <- power.t.test(
  n = n_min - 1,
  delta = mean_diff,
  sd = sd_diff_formula,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  type = "paired",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("At n =", n_min, ": power =", round(result_min$power, 6), 
    "[meets target:", result_min$power >= target_power, "]\n")
cat("At n =", n_min - 1, ": power =", round(result_prev$power, 6), 
    "[meets target:", result_prev$power >= target_power, "]\n")

# Verify null hypothesis calibration
# At n = 21, what is the Type I error rate under H0?

library(jsonlite)

mean_diff <- 3
sd_baseline <- 5
sd_followup <- 5.5
rho <- 0.5
sd_diff <- sqrt(sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2*rho*sd_baseline*sd_followup)

cat("=== NULL HYPOTHESIS CALIBRATION ===\n")
cat("Testing that alpha = 0.05 (one-sided) is maintained at n = 21\n\n")

# Under H0: true mean difference = 0 (not 3 kg)
# The test should reject with probability exactly α = 0.05
n_test <- 21
df <- n_test - 1

# One-sided test: reject if t > t_crit
t_crit <- qt(1 - 0.05, df)  # critical value for one-sided α = 0.05
cat("Critical value for n = 21, one-sided α = 0.05:\n")
cat("t_crit = qt(0.95,", df, ") =", round(t_crit, 6), "\n\n")

# Type I error: probability of rejecting H0 when it's true
# Under H0 (Δ = 0), the test statistic follows t(df) with ncp = 0
type_i_error <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = 0)
cat("Type I error P(T > t_crit | H0 true):\n")
cat("P(T >", round(t_crit, 6), "| df =", df, ", ncp = 0)\n")
cat("= 1 - P(T ≤", round(t_crit, 6), ")\n")
cat("=", type_i_error, "\n")
cat("Expected: 0.05\n")
cat("Match: ", isTRUE(abs(type_i_error - 0.05) < 1e-6), "\n\n")

# Verify one-sided vs two-sided distinction
cat("=== VERIFY ONE-SIDED TEST ===\n")
cat("One-sided (H1: Δ > 0):\n")
result_one <- power.t.test(
  n = 21,
  delta = 3,
  sd = sd_diff,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  type = "paired",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)
cat("  Power at n=21:", round(result_one$power, 6), "\n")

cat("Two-sided (H1: Δ ≠ 0):\n")
result_two <- power.t.test(
  n = 21,
  delta = 3,
  sd = sd_diff,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  type = "paired",
  alternative = "two.sided"
)
cat("  Power at n=21:", round(result_two$power, 6), "\n")
cat("  (Should be lower than one-sided for same α and n)\n\n")

# Verify the effect size interpretation
cat("=== EFFECT SIZE INTERPRETATION ===\n")
cat("For a paired t-test:\n")
cat("- Effect size is the difference divided by the SD of differences\n")
cat("- Mean difference: 3 kg\n")
cat("- SD of differences: √(5² + 5.5² − 2×0.5×5×5.5) = 5.267827 kg\n")
cat("- Cohen's d = 3 / 5.267827 = 0.5694948\n")
cat("- This is a MEDIUM effect size (Cohen: d > 0.5)\n\n")

# Using alternative approach and detailed formula checks

# Given parameters
mean_diff <- 3        # kg (hypothesized mean weight reduction)
sd_baseline <- 5      # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5    # kg
rho <- 0.5            # within-person correlation
alpha <- 0.05         # one-sided significance level
target_power <- 0.80

# Step 1: Verify SD of differences formula
# For paired differences: σ_diff = √(σ₀² + σ₁² − 2ρσ₀σ₁)
sd_diff_formula <- sqrt(sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2*rho*sd_baseline*sd_followup)
cat("Step 1: SD of paired differences\n")
cat("Formula: σ_diff = √(σ₀² + σ₁² − 2ρσ₀σ₁)\n")
cat("Calculation: √(5² + 5.5² − 2×0.5×5×5.5)\n")
cat("           = √(25 + 30.25 − 27.5)\n")
cat("           = √27.75\n")
cat("Result: σ_diff =", sd_diff_formula, "kg\n\n")

# Step 2: Calculate Cohen's d
cohen_d <- mean_diff / sd_diff_formula
cat("Step 2: Effect size (Cohen's d for paired design)\n")
cat("Cohen's d = 3 / ", sd_diff_formula, " =", cohen_d, "\n\n")

# Step 3: Manual power calculation using non-central t-distribution
# For one-sided test at α = 0.05:
# Critical value t_crit from standard t distribution with (n-1) df
# Non-centrality parameter: λ = d * √n = (mean_diff / sd_diff) * √n

# Test for various sample sizes to find minimum meeting target power
cat("Step 3: Power calculation across sample sizes\n")
cat("n\tCritical t\tNon-centrality λ\tPower (via pt)\n")
cat(strrep("-", 60), "\n")

powers_manual <- data.frame(n = integer(), power = numeric())

for (n in 18:23) {
  df <- n - 1  # degrees of freedom for one-sample/paired t-test
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)  # one-sided critical value (upper tail)
  lambda <- cohen_d * sqrt(n)   # non-centrality parameter
  
  # Power = P(T > t_crit | λ) = 1 - P(T ≤ t_crit | λ)
  # where T ~ t(df, λ) non-central t-distribution
  power_manual <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  
  powers_manual <- rbind(powers_manual, 
                         data.frame(n = n, power = power_manual))
  
  cat(n, "\t", round(t_crit, 4), "\t\t",

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Paired t-test sample size calculation
# H0: mean weight reduction = 0 vs H1: mean weight reduction = 3 kg
# One-sided test, alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.80

# Parameters
mean_diff <- 3        # kg - hypothesized mean weight reduction
sd_baseline <- 5      # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5    # kg
rho <- 0.5            # within-person correlation

# Calculate SD of paired differences
# σ_diff = √(σ₀² + σ₁² − 2ρσ₀σ₁)
sd_diff <- sqrt(sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2*rho*sd_baseline*sd_followup)
cat("SD of paired differences:", sd_diff, "kg\n")

# Effect size (Cohen's d for paired t-test)
cohen_d <- mean_diff / sd_diff
cat("Cohen's d:", cohen_d, "\n\n")

# For one-sided paired t-test: n = 2 * (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 / d^2
# where z_alpha is critical value for one-sided test at alpha level
# and z_beta is critical value for (1-power)
# But for small samples, use exact t-distribution approach via power.t.test

# Try using stats::power.t.test for paired t-test
# This function can invert to find sample size

# For a paired t-test with power.t.test:
# - type = "paired" for paired test
# - delta = effect size (mean difference)
# - sd = SD of differences
# - sig.level = alpha
# - power = target power
# - alternative = "one.sided"

result_80 <- power.t.test(
  n = NULL,           # We're solving for n
  delta = mean_diff,  # Effect size (mean difference)
  sd = sd_diff,       # SD of paired differences
  sig.level = 0.05,   # One-sided alpha
  power = 0.80,       # Target power
  type = "paired",    # Paired t-test
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

print(result_80)
cat("\nContinuous solution (n):", result_80$n, "\n")

# Since we need integer participants, round up
n_rounded <- ceiling(result_80$n)
cat("Rounded up to integer:", n_rounded, "\n\n")

# Verify the achieved power at the rounded sample size
power_achieved <- power.t.test(
  n = n_rounded,
  delta = mean_diff,
  sd = sd_diff,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  type = "paired",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("ACHIEVED POWER at n =", n_rounded, ":", power_achieved$power, "\n")

# Also check the previous integer (n-1) to confirm it doesn't meet target
if(n_rounded > 1) {
  power_prev <- power.t.test(
    n = n_rounded - 1,
    delta = mean_diff,
    sd = sd_diff,
    sig.level = 0.05,
    type = "paired",
    alternative = "one.sided"
  )
  cat("Power at n =", n_rounded - 1, ":", power_prev$power, "\n")
}

# Summary
cat("\n=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size:", n_rounded, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_achieved$power, 4), "\n")
cat("Target power: 0.80\n")
cat("Meets target:", power_achieved$power >= 0.80, "\n")


# Evidence e2; success=true

# Final verification and structured output
library(jsonlite)

# Parameters recap

sd_baseline <- 5
sd_followup <- 5.5
rho <- 0.5

# SD of differences calculation

# Sample size calculation - inversion

  n = NULL,
  delta = mean_diff,
  sd = sd_diff,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  power = 0.80,
  type = "paired",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

n_continuous <- result_80$n
n_integer <- ceiling(n_continuous)

# Achieved power at minimum integer sample size
power_at_n <- power.t.test(
  n = n_integer,
  delta = mean_diff,
  sd = sd_diff,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  type = "paired",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

# Power at preceding admissible design (n-1)
power_at_n_minus_1 <- power.t.test(
  n = n_integer - 1,
  delta = mean_diff,
  sd = sd_diff,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  type = "paired",

# Structured output
results <- list(
  sample_size = n_integer,
  achieved_power = power_at_n,

  continuous_solution = n_continuous,

)

cat(toJSON(list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_integer, unit = "participants_total")
  )
), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
cat("\n")

# Additional verification output
cat("\n=== VERIFICATION DETAILS ===\n")
cat("Continuous solution: n =", n_continuous, "participants\n")
cat("Rounded to integer:  n =", n_integer, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_integer, ":", round(power_at_n, 6), "\n")
